examples.en: I'm going to take my physical exam next month.
I got a grade 3 result at the physical exam.
The date for the physical exam came out, so I took a day off.
My older brother went to the hospital because of his physical exam.

examples.ko: 신검을 받기 전에 밥을 먹지 말래요.
examples.en: They say not to eat before the physical exam.

examples.ko: 친구는 신검 결과가 좋아서 현역으로 가요.
examples.en: My friend's physical exam result was good, so he is going to active duty.

explain: '신체검사'의 줄임말로, 주로 군대에 가기 전에 받는 검사를 말할 때 써요. 학교나 회사의 건강검진에는 보통 '건강검진'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: We have a physical examination at school tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신검'의 원래 말이고, 군대뿐 아니라 학교나 회사에서도 두루 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the full form of 신검 and is used for school and work as well as the military.

phrases.en: My younger brother is getting his physical exam next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: '받다'와 함께 써서 검사를 받는 사람의 입장에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 받다 to talk about the person taking the exam.

phrases.en: The physical exam results came out today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 검사를 받은 뒤 나온 판정이나 등급을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the grade or result after the exam.

explain_en: Clipped, colloquial form of 신체검사 (e.g. 군대 신검), common in talk about military or school checkups. It is short for '신체검사' and is mostly used for the exam taken before military service. For school or work checkups people usually say '건강검진'.

t90.ax: I got a grade 3 result at the physical exam.

en: to go and return; to make a round trip

examples.en: I go back and forth between home and work by bus every day.
I made a round trip between Seoul and Busan in a day.
The shuttle bus runs back and forth between the station and the school.

examples.ko: 차로 한 시간이면 왕복할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can make the round trip in an hour by car.
A round trip on foot takes about two hours.

examples.ko: 도서관을 왕복하는 길에 꽃이 많이 피었어요.
examples.en: Many flowers bloomed along the way to and from the library.

explain: '왕복'은 '편도'와 짝이에요. 표를 살 때 '왕복 표 주세요', '편도로 주세요'라고 말해요. 동사 '왕복하다'는 '오가다'보다 딱딱하고, 거리와 시간을 말할 때 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 부산행 왕복 표 한 장 주세요.
phrases.en: One round-trip ticket to Busan, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표를 살 때 '편도'와 구별해서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when buying tickets, in contrast to 편도.

phrases.example: 집에서 학교까지 왕복 두 시간 걸려요.
phrases.en: It takes two hours round trip from home to school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가고 오는 데 걸리는 시간이나 거리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the time or distance of going and coming back.

phrases.en: I often go back and forth between the two cities.
phrases.nuance_ko: '왕복하다'보다 부드럽고 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer and more everyday than 왕복하다.

explain_en: A set trip out and back, like commuting; neutral and countable. '왕복' is the pair of '편도' (one way); when buying tickets you say '왕복 표 주세요' or '편도로 주세요'. The verb '왕복하다' is stiffer than '오가다' and is often used when talking about distance and time.

examples.ko: 남은 고기를 은박지로 싸서 냉장고에 넣었어요.
examples.en: I wrapped the leftover meat in foil and put it in the fridge.
I wrapped the sweet potatoes in foil and baked them in the oven.

examples.ko: 은박지가 다 떨어져서 마트에서 새로 사 왔어요.
examples.en: We ran out of foil, so I bought some at the supermarket.
You must not put foil in the microwave.

examples.ko: 소풍 갈 때 엄마가 김밥을 은박지에 싸 주셔서 편했어요.
examples.en: It was convenient that Mom wrapped the gimbap in foil for the picnic.

examples.ko: 접시 위에 은박지를 덮어 두면 음식이 덜 말라요.
examples.en: If you cover the plate with foil, the food dries out less.

explain: 부엌에서는 '호일'이나 '알루미늄 호일'이라고 말하는 사람도 많아요. 음식을 싸거나 굽거나 덮을 때 써요. 전자레인지에는 넣지 않는 게 좋아요.

phrases.en: I wrap the meat in foil and grill it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부엌에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More commonly used in the kitchen.

phrases.en: I laid foil on the oven tray.
phrases.nuance_ko: 굽기 전에 판 위에 펼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when spreading it on a tray before baking.

phrases.en: Cover the leftover food with foil.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 덮어서 보관할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when covering food to store it.

explain_en: Many people also say '호일' or '알루미늄 호일' in the kitchen. You use it to wrap, bake or cover food. It is best not to put it in a microwave.

examples.en: That player was traded to another team.
There is a lot of trade news this year.
I heard the manager opposed the trade.

examples.ko: 트레이드로 온 선수가 첫 경기에서 활약했어요.
examples.en: The player who came by trade played well in his first game.

examples.ko: 두 팀은 선수 두 명씩 트레이드하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The two teams agreed to trade two players each.
The trade deadline is approaching.

explain: 한국어 '트레이드'는 주로 야구·농구 같은 프로 스포츠에서 선수를 다른 팀과 맞바꾸는 일이에요. 영어 trade-off(서로 얻고 잃음)와 뜻이 달라요. 보통 '트레이드되다/트레이드하다'로 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 투수는 시즌 중에 다른 팀으로 트레이드됐어요.
phrases.en: That pitcher was traded to another team during the season.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선수가 주어일 때 쓰는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, used when the player is the subject.

phrases.en: The club traded two players.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팀이 선수를 맞바꿀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a team swaps players.

phrases.example: 그 선수가 트레이드 대상이라는 소문이 있어요.
phrases.en: There's a rumor that player is a trade target.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맞바꿀 수 있는 선수를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a player who might be traded.

explain_en: In Korean, 트레이드 mainly means swapping players between teams in pro sports like baseball and basketball. It does not mean the English 'trade-off'. It is usually used as 트레이드되다 or 트레이드하다.

examples.en: How much is the one-way fare from Seoul to Busan?
Shall I buy a one-way ticket or a round-trip one?
It takes about an hour one way to the airport.

examples.ko: 저는 학교까지 편도 삼십 분 거리에 살아요.
examples.en: I live thirty minutes one way from school.

examples.ko: 돌아올 때는 차로 올 거라서 편도 표만 샀어요.
examples.en: I'll come back by car, so I bought only a one-way ticket.

examples.ko: 제주도 가는 편도 항공권이 오늘 싸졌어요.
examples.en: One-way flights to Jeju got cheaper today.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '왕복'이에요. 표를 살 때 '편도예요, 왕복이에요?'라고 자주 물어봐요. 출퇴근 거리를 말할 때도 '편도 한 시간'처럼 가는 쪽만 세요.

phrases.en: It's a bit cheaper if you buy a round trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: '편도'의 짝이 되는 말이에요. 가고 오는 것을 모두 포함해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The counterpart of 편도; it covers going and coming back.

phrases.en: The one-way fare to the airport is 10,000 won.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가는 쪽만 계산한 값을 말할 때 써요. 표를 살 때 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The price for just one direction; often heard when buying tickets.

phrases.en: It takes one hour one way to get to work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 출퇴근 거리를 말할 때 가는 쪽만 세는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A way to give a commute time counting only one direction.

explain_en: Its partner word is '왕복' (round trip). When you buy a ticket, you'll often hear '편도예요, 왕복이에요?'. For commutes, Koreans also count only one direction, as in '편도 한 시간'.

examples.en: A company sponsored this concert.
The sponsoring company's name appears on the screen.
A famous brand provides the costumes for the drama.

examples.ko: 가게 사장님이 행사 상품을 협찬해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The shop owner kindly donated prizes for the event.

examples.ko: 우리 학교 축제를 협찬할 회사를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: We are looking for a company to sponsor our school festival.
I thank the people who sponsored the event.

explain: '후원하다'는 돈이나 도움을 주며 응원하는 것이고, '협찬하다'는 회사가 물건이나 돈을 대 주고 대신 이름을 알리는 거래의 느낌이 있어요. 방송 자막의 '의상 협찬'처럼 방송·행사에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: The drama received clothing sponsorship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도움을 받는 쪽에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side that receives the support.

phrases.en: The sponsors' names appear at the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이나 돈을 대 준 회사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The company that provided goods or money.

phrases.en: The company sponsored drinks for the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주는 쪽에서 쓰는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side that gives the support.

explain_en: '후원하다' is giving money or help to support someone; '협찬하다' has a business-exchange feel, where a company provides goods or funds in return for publicity. You often see it in broadcast credits like '의상 협찬' (costumes provided by).

examples.en: Try sounding out what that person really thinks.

examples.ko: 월급을 물어보며 내 마음을 떠보는 것 같았어요.
examples.en: It seemed like he was testing me by asking about my salary.

examples.ko: 친구가 일부러 말을 걸어 나를 떠봤어요.
examples.en: My friend deliberately talked to me to feel me out.
I pretended not to know to test out the price.
Stop testing me and tell me honestly.
It feels bad when you keep probing me.

explain: 상대의 속마음이나 생각을 알아내려고 슬쩍 말이나 행동으로 시험해 볼 때 써요. '눈을 떠 보다'처럼 '뜨다'와 '보다'를 띄어 쓰는 말과는 달라요. 듣는 사람은 기분이 나쁠 수 있어서 '떠보지 마세요'처럼 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: Please don't hint around and try to sound me out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 속마음을 알아내려는 것이 싫을 때 부탁하거나 말릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you dislike that someone is probing your real thoughts.
phrases.en_equiv: don't try to sound me out

phrases.example: 친구가 내 마음을 떠보려고 질문을 했어요.
phrases.en: My friend asked a question to sound out my feelings.
phrases.nuance_ko: '떠보다'와 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation with 떠보다.

phrases.en: I casually sounded out whether the price would go up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '슬쩍'을 붙이면 눈치 못 채게 조심스럽게 시험해 본다는 느낌이 더해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '슬쩍' adds the sense of testing carefully without being noticed.

explain_en: Casual spoken; subtly testing someone's real feelings. It is used when you subtly test someone with words or actions to find out what they really think. It differs from '눈을 떠 보다', where '뜨다' and '보다' are written separately. The other person may feel bad, so people often say '떠보지 마세요'.

t90.ax: Stop testing me and tell me honestly.

en: owner of a shop or restaurant

examples.en: The restaurant owner greeted the customers.

examples.ko: 가게 업주는 요즘 손님이 줄어서 걱정이에요.
examples.en: The shop owner is worried because customers have decreased lately.
The business owners asked the government for help.

examples.ko: 이 미용실은 업주가 직접 머리를 잘라 줘요.
examples.en: At this hair salon the owner cuts the hair himself.
The owner and the staff cleaned together.
Rents went up, so business owners are having a hard time.

explain: '업주'는 식당, 가게, 숙박업소 같은 장사를 하는 주인을 부르는 말이라 뉴스나 서류에서 자주 나와요. 말로 직접 부를 때는 '사장님'이라고 해요. 직원은 '종업원'이에요.

phrases.en: The business owners gathered and talked about the new rules.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-들'을 붙여 여러 명의 업주를 말해요. 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -들 refers to several owners. Common in news.

phrases.example: 문제가 있으면 먼저 업주에게 말해 보세요.
phrases.en: If there is a problem, try telling the owner first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '-에게'를 붙인 쓰임이에요. 말로 직접 부를 때는 '사장님'을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the particle -에게. When addressing someone directly, use 사장님.

phrases.en: Boss, could I have some water here?
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당이나 가게에서 주인을 직접 부를 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word used to address a shop or restaurant owner directly.

explain_en: Formal; owner of a shop or restaurant, often in news. '업주' is the owner of a restaurant, shop, or lodging business, and is common in the news and on paperwork. When you speak to the person directly, you call them '사장님'. Their staff are '종업원'.

t90.ax: The owner and the staff cleaned together.

examples.ko: 중개업자가 좋은 집을 몇 군데 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: The agent showed me a few good houses.
I made an appointment with an agent to find a house.

examples.ko: 믿을 수 있는 중개업자를 찾는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: It is important to find an agent you can trust.
How much commission do I have to pay the agent?

examples.ko: 중개업자한테 전화해서 집을 보러 가기로 했어요.
examples.en: I called the agent and decided to go see the house.

examples.ko: 그 중개업자는 설명을 자세히 해 줘서 고마웠어요.
examples.en: I was grateful that the agent explained things in detail.

explain: 집이나 물건 같은 거래를 연결해 주는 사람을 가리키는 말이에요. 집을 구할 때는 보통 '공인중개사', '부동산 사장님'이라고 더 많이 말해요. '중개업자'는 글이나 뉴스에서 조금 딱딱하게 나와요.

phrases.en: The licensed agent helped with the house contract.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자격증이 있는 중개업자를 말하며 집 구할 때 가장 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a licensed agent, the most common term when finding a home.

phrases.en: I found a house through an agent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누구의 도움으로 거래했는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say whose help you used to make a deal.

phrases.en: I paid a fee to the agent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거래가 끝나고 돈을 줄 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for paying money after a deal is done.

explain_en: Business person who arranges deals, as in real estate. It refers to a person who connects both sides of a deal, such as for a house or goods. When looking for a home, people more often say '공인중개사' or '부동산 사장님'. '중개업자' sounds a bit stiff and appears more in writing and news.

t90.ax: The agent showed me a few good houses.

en: to compromise; to meet halfway; to give in

examples.en: We compromised with each other on the price.
Both sides give in a little and reach a compromise.
I never compromise on quality.
In the end, we decided to meet in the middle.
The couple settled on a moving date and signed the contract.

examples.ko: 쉽게 타협하면 나중에 후회할 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you compromise too easily, you may regret it later.

explain: 서로 조금씩 양보해서 합의에 이를 때 써요. 비슷한 '합의하다'는 결과에, '타협하다'는 서로 물러서는 과정에 초점이 있어요. 원칙을 쉽게 버리는 느낌이 있어서 '타협하지 않다'는 자기 기준을 지킨다는 칭찬이 되기도 해요.

phrases.en: settle for what is realistic
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 하고 싶던 일을 접고 형편에 맞게 선택한다는 뜻이에요. 조금 씁쓸한 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means giving up what you really wanted and choosing what fits your circumstances, with a slightly bitter feeling.

explain_en: Each side concedes to end a conflict; can imply giving up principles. Use it when both sides give a little and reach agreement. '합의하다' focuses on the result, while '타협하다' focuses on the process of both sides backing off. It can feel like dropping principles too easily, so '타협하지 않다' can be praise for holding your standards.

en: to conciliate; to appease; to coax

examples.en: I talked my friend around and brought him onto the same team.
The boss tried to win over the employee who wanted to leave with money.

examples.ko: 아무리 회유해도 그 사람은 마음을 안 바꿔요.
examples.en: No matter how much you coax him, he won't change his mind.
I bought the child a snack to coax him.
It seems the other side is trying to win us over.
Coaxing or threatening people is not right.

explain: '사람을 회유하다'처럼 목적어는 사람이에요. '설득하다'는 중립적이지만 '회유하다'는 이익이나 달콤한 말로 꾀어 내 편으로 만들려는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: He tried to win over the people who opposed him.
phrases.nuance_ko: '회유하다'에 '-려고 하다'를 붙여 설득하거나 꾀어 보려는 시도를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-려고 하다' to '회유하다' shows an attempt to coax or win someone over.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 회유에 넘어가서 마음을 바꿨어요.
phrases.en: He fell for the coaxing and changed his mind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회유당하는 사람 입장에서 말할 때 써요. 달콤한 말이나 이익에 마음이 흔들렸다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the target's side, meaning someone was swayed by sweet words or benefits.

phrases.en: They tried to coax me with sweet words.
phrases.nuance_ko: '회유하다'가 어떤 방법을 쓰는지 보여 주는 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation showing the typical method of coaxing.

explain_en: The object is a person, as in '사람을 회유하다'. '설득하다' is neutral, but '회유하다' suggests luring someone to your side with benefits or sweet words.

examples.en: If you pay late, a surcharge is added.
If you have a certificate, you get bonus points.
An extra amount was added to the tax.
The amount rose a lot because an addition was applied.
Night work comes with an added allowance.

examples.ko: 이 경우에는 가산 없이 그대로 계산해요.
examples.en: In this case, we calculate it as it is, with nothing added.

explain: '가산'은 원래 금액이나 점수에 따로 더하는 것을 말해요. 일반 '더하기'가 아니라 규칙에 따라 붙는 추가분이라는 느낌이에요. '가산점', '가산세', '가산 수당'처럼 다른 말과 붙여 써요.

phrases.en: You get bonus points if you do volunteer work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기본 점수에 더해 주는 점수를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Points added on top of a base score.

phrases.example: 세금을 늦게 내면 가산세를 내야 해요.
phrases.en: If you pay your taxes late, you have to pay a surcharge tax.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기한을 어겼을 때 원래 세금에 더해서 내는 세금이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An extra tax added to the original one when a deadline is missed.

phrases.en: If you work at night, you get an extra allowance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 야간이나 휴일 근무처럼 규칙에 따라 더 주는 돈을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Extra pay given by rule, such as for night or holiday work.

explain_en: Extra added on to a tax or fee — formal, finance (가산세) '가산' is an amount or score added on top of the original one. Rather than plain addition, it feels like an extra portion applied by a rule. It forms terms like '가산점' (bonus points), '가산세' (penalty tax), and '가산 수당' (premium pay).

t90.ax: An extra amount was added to the tax.

examples.en: How much is the gym's membership fee?
You pay the joining fee only once at the start.
The joining fee is free this month.
If you pay the joining fee, we give you a coupon.
The club's joining fee is 10,000 won.
I'm hesitating to join because of the joining fee.

explain: 모임이나 회원제에 처음 들어갈 때 한 번 내는 돈이에요. 달마다 내는 '회비', '월 이용료'와 달라요. '가입비 면제'나 '가입비 무료'는 광고에서 자주 봐요.

phrases.en: I paid the membership fee to join the club.
phrases.nuance_ko: '내다'와 함께 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic pairing, with the verb '내다'.

phrases.example: 이번 달에는 가입비 면제 행사를 해요.
phrases.en: This month there is an event waiving the membership fee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광고나 안내문에서 자주 보는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often seen in ads and notices.

phrases.en: This app has no membership fee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 내지 않고 가입할 수 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you can join without paying.

explain_en: One-time fee paid when joining. It is the one-time payment when you first join a club or membership. It differs from '회비' or '월 이용료', which are paid regularly. '가입비 면제' and '가입비 무료' are common in ads.

t90.ax: The joining fee is free this month.

examples.en: New students get their first-semester tuition reduced.
The city decided to reduce taxes for small business owners.
They reduce water bills for low-income households.

examples.ko: 올해부터 감면할 수 있는 세금이 늘었어요.
examples.en: From this year, more taxes can be reduced.

examples.ko: 서류를 내면 수업료를 감면받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you submit the documents, you can get your fees reduced.
They cut the parking fee for this month only.

explain: 세금, 등록금, 요금처럼 내야 하는 돈을 줄여 주거나 아예 안 받는다는 말이에요. 전부 안 내는 '면제하다'와 달리 일부를 줄여 주는 경우까지 넓게 써요. 혜택을 받는 사람은 '감면받다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: They reduce the entrance fee for students.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요금을 줄이거나 안 받을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a fee is reduced or waived.

phrases.en: I received a reduction in my tuition.
phrases.nuance_ko: 혜택을 받는 사람 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the point of view of the person receiving the benefit.

phrases.en: The university waives tuition for scholarship students.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부가 아니라 전부 안 받는다는 점이 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: Differs in that the whole amount is waived, not just part.

explain_en: Verb — grant a cut or waiver of fees (수업료를 감면하다) It is used for money you owe, such as taxes, tuition and fees, when it is reduced or waived. Unlike '면제하다', which means not paying at all, it also covers partial reductions. The person receiving the benefit uses '감면받다'.

gh: formal; make amounts or levels drop

p.n: 인하하다 lowers the rate or price; 감면하다 reduces or waives what is owed.

examples.en: I prepared documents to apply for a reduction in my insurance premium.
This reduction applies from next month.

examples.ko: 지원금 감액이 되면 생활이 많이 힘들어져요.
examples.en: If the subsidy is reduced, life gets much harder.

examples.ko: 감액에 이의가 있으면 이번 주 안에 말해 주세요.
examples.en: If you object to the reduction, please tell us this week.
I was surprised that the reduction was bigger than I expected.
The reduced fine eased my burden a little.

explain: 보험료, 수당, 벌금처럼 정해진 돈의 액수를 줄이는 일이에요. 반대말은 '증액'이고, 공문서나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: This month's allowance is subject to reduction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈이 줄어드는 항목이나 사람을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to items or people whose amount will be reduced.

phrases.en: I got notice from the company that my allowance would be reduced.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄어든다는 사실을 공식적으로 알릴 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for officially notifying that an amount is cut.

phrases.en: It will be increased next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '감액'의 반대말로, 돈의 액수를 늘리는 일이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 감액: increasing an amount of money.

explain_en: Formal word for reducing a payment or fee amount (수업료 감액). It refers to lowering a fixed amount of money, such as insurance premiums, allowances or fines. Its opposite is '증액', and it often appears in official documents and the news.

t90.ax: This reduction applies from next month.
